intent: THE GATE OBLIGATION — human gates are the engine's load-bearing decision points (flow-control-spec §3: "every step stops and waits") and today they are enforced by NOTHING but event ORDER. The verified finding: (1) the store's only gate rule is sequence — gateProblems checks that a completed has an earlier confirmed(grill) and that confirm never precedes grill, and nothing checks WHO decided or that a presentation intervened, so created → submitted grill → confirmed grill, all by an AGENT at spawn, satisfies the rule — and the rule REWARDS accepting at spawn (the compliant path is the ungated path); (2) a task spawned and never submitted is INVISIBLE — spawn! writes only created (so the task derives queued), and undecidedEverywhere/LookBack.pendingGates collect only UNDECIDED submitted events, so ann next proposes it frontmost-ready with NO pending gate; (3) the frame's stop fires only for tasks driven THROUGH the frame — a pre-accepted grill skips the gate WRITE but not the step (frame.ts: state 'confirmed' → skip the write, re-run the step), and implementation tasks have no content steps, so an accepted entry gate is a pure pass-through; (4) nothing is human-only — the engine's single initiator check is goal! met's refusal of the 'agent' default; gate! has no who/interactivity/presentation check and the frame's interactive seam has no TTY check (grep isTTY → nothing), so `echo accept | ann run!` is a legal "human gate" carrying no identity. This epic makes the gate obligation MACHINE-VISIBLE and HUMAN-ONLY: the entry gate exists from spawn, a gate write requires a recorded human initiator, the frame can only LAND on a gate card (never decide one), and a check rule makes the regression detectable.
acceptanceCriteria: FIX-1 — THE ENTRY GATE BECOMES MACHINE-VISIBLE: `spawn!` ends by recording `submitted @ grill` through the EXISTING `submit!` path (no new mechanism, no new write path), so a freshly spawned task DERIVES blocked and appears in `ann next`'s pendingGates; `run!`/`advance!` then stop at blocked-at-gate until a decision exists. Verified by a spawn→next test showing the pending grill gate and a run! that stops before any execute step

FIX-2 — GATE WRITES BECOME HUMAN-ONLY: `gate!` refuses an automated initiator exactly as `goal! met` does (the human-only refusal generalised; at minimum the grill gate, with the confirm-gate posture DECIDED and recorded on the task rather than left implicit); the gate write requires RECORDED_BY and fails closed on the 'agent' default, stamping the recorded human as the decider

FIX-3 — THE FRAME'S INTERACTIVE SEAM IS FIXED: the frame's gate path refuses NON-TTY stdin (`echo accept | ann run!` is never a gate decision), carries the HUMAN identity from the interact channel into the gate write on a real TTY, and — for the operator path — run!/advance! LAND on a blocked-at-gate card for the human to `gate!` instead of the frame writing submit!+gate! on the human's behalf

FIX-4 — THE DISCIPLINE IS PINNED TO THE HUMAN, NOT THE OPERATOR: AGENTS.md states it — the operator presents the gate card; ONLY the human runs gate!; no agent (operator included) records a gate decision for the human; and the spawn ritual ends at submit! grill + the card, never 'spawned + grill accepted'

FIX-5 — THE DETECTION IS SCRIPTED, SO IT CANNOT REGRESS SILENTLY: a check/verify rule flags an agent-initiated gate decision (or a confirmed(grill) landing in the same write burst as created with no intervening presentation); the rule ships with tests and is registered in the derived check-rules registry — not stated only as prose

VERIFICATION: the full suite stays green (new tests per fix — spawn→blocked, the gate! human-only refusal, the non-TTY refusal, the check rule), `ann check`/`ann verify` stay clean on the live journey, the affected contracts are amended (flow-control-spec §3 gate obligation + the resource-registry reconciliation register), and the work is committed with evidence
